column1: # The 144 specified mutation obligations of P01–P22, enumerated.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS BESIDE register.tsv
# build/proof/register.tsv enumerates the twenty-two PROOF TESTS and counts
# their mutants. It does not name them. So "P17 has 0 of 19" is auditable as
# arithmetic and not as evidence: nothing in the repository said which nineteen,
# what each one changes, or what is supposed to catch it.
# This file is that enumeration, one row per specified mutation, and it is the
# single source of truth for the mutation set. docs/testing-strategy.md §4
# carries the tables for P01–P15; §4.3 states that P16–P22 "are specified in
# full by their owning ADRs and are cited here, not restated", so their sixty-
# A catalogue built from testing-strategy.md alone is sixty-four rows short and
# looks complete, which is exactly the failure this file exists to prevent.
# MUTATION and EXPECTED_ORACLE are transcribed VERBATIM from those tables' two
# columns (rule PT-4: a consumed conformance surface is not re-derived). Only
# §4.3: "M-P20-3 (remove-then-add instead of atomic swap) is THE SAME MUTANT as
# M-P09-3, declared as shared so it is not counted twice as independent
# evidence." Both ids are rows here, because dropping one breaks the count §4
# calls load-bearing; M-P20-3 carries STATUS `SHARED-WITH:M-P09-3` so that one
# patch can never be counted as two pieces of evidence.
# The per-proof counts reconcile with register.tsv's MUT_SPEC column exactly:
# build/proof/mutation-gate.sh asserts that reconciliation on every run.
# THE STATUS VOCABULARY — AND WHY THERE IS NO WORD THAT COULD BE MISREAD
# A specification entry with no executable implementation is UNDISCHARGED. It is
# not a pass, it is not a skip, and it must never be counted alongside a killed
# mutant. STATUS here is the IMPLEMENTATION state; the EXECUTION verdict
# (killed / survived / timeout / unviable / not-executed) is decided by
# build/proof/run-mutants.sh at run time and reported by mutation-gate.sh, which
# also fails if the two disagree.
#   IMPLEMENTED           a patch for this id exists in build/mutants/. OWNER
#                         names the workspace and the cargo command that must
#                         fail against it. Whether it is actually KILLED is the
#                         run's verdict, never this file's claim.
#   SHARED-WITH:<id>      §4.3 declares this obligation to be the same mutant as
#                         <id>. One patch, one piece of evidence, two rows.
#   MISSING-UNIMPLEMENTED no patch exists, and the OWNING PROOF TEST has at
#                         least one evidence command that runs on a plain Linux
#                         runner. That is a triage hint about the proof, NOT a
#                         claim that this particular mutant is catchable by it:
#                         the NEEDS column is the authority on what is absent,
#                         and for most of these rows it names infrastructure the
#                         runner does not have. UNDISCHARGED either way.
#   MISSING-NO-ORACLE     no patch exists and the owning proof test has no
#                         runnable evidence command at all, or this row's NEEDS
#                         names the specific missing assertion that was checked
#                         against the code and found unable to see the defect.
# Both MISSING states count identically in every total mutation-gate.sh prints.
# The split exists so the next person knows where to start, not so one of them
# NEEDS is per-row where this catalogue's author verified the reason against the
# code and the candidate oracle; otherwise it is the owning register row's NEEDS
# column, which is that proof test's own statement of what is absent.
#   ID  PROOF  COMPONENT  REQUIREMENT  MUTATION  EXPECTED_ORACLE  OWNER  STATUS  NEEDS
